basic_information.official_title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR 7 DAYS FORFEITABLE BEREAVEMENT LEAVE PRIVILEGES ANNUALLY WITH PAY TO EMPLOYEES IN THE PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTORS WITHIN THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation within the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Gives every employee in the region — public or private, whatever their employment status — 7 days of paid leave each year when an immediate family member dies.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The act declares that the Bangsamoro Government recognises the unique and societal aspects of bereavement and shall foster a workplace culture that upholds the welfare of its people.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Seven working days of paid bereavement leave a year becomes a legal entitlement. An application not acted on within five working days is automatically approved, and using the leave cannot be a ground for dismissal, demotion or a bad performance rating.
who_will_be_affected: Every employee in an employer-employee relationship in the BARMM, public or private
Employers, who must grant the leave — except small and micro enterprises, which are exempt
Employees who have lost a spouse, parent, parent-in-law, child, ward or full-blood sibling
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2025 — 15 days after publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. If an immediate family member dies, you get 7 days of paid leave. Weekends and holidays don't count against it. If your employer sits on the application for five working days, it is automatically approved.
in_practice: 7 days of bereavement leave with pay, each year
Saturdays, Sundays and holidays are excluded from the count — so it is seven working days
Available to any employee regardless of employment status, in the public or private sector
Unused leave does not carry over and cannot be converted to cash
An application not acted upon within five working days is deemed approved
Taking the leave cannot be a ground for termination, constructive dismissal, demotion, or an unsatisfactory performance rating

for_specific_groups.Private sector employees: You are covered, unless your employer is a small or micro enterprise. Complaints about unjustified denial go to the Minister of Labor and Employment, decided through summary proceedings.
for_specific_groups.Government employees: You are covered. Complaints against responsible officers follow the Revised Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service.
for_specific_groups.Employees of small and micro enterprises: Section 4 exempts these entities from granting the leave — this is the main gap in coverage.
for_specific_groups.Employees with more than one spouse: Section 5 says 'legitimate spouse/s' in the plural, so a marriage recognised under Muslim personal law is within the definition.
for_specific_groups.Contractual and casual staff: 'Regardless of employment status' — the entitlement does not depend on being permanent.

what_you_can_do: Apply in writing and note the date your employer received it — after five working days without action it is deemed approved
Have documentation ready: the employer may require a death certificate, obituary, or proof of relationship
If refused without justification, complain to the Minister of Labor and Employment (private sector) or use the civil service administrative route (public sector)
Check whether an existing company or agency benefit is more generous — this act does not reduce it
watch_out_for: Small and micro enterprises are exempt, which excludes a large share of the region's workforce.
The leave is forfeitable — unused days do not accumulate and cannot be cashed out.
Only full-blood siblings count; half-siblings and step-siblings are not in the definition.
The act sets no penalty on an employer beyond the complaint and administrative routes.

key_terms_explained.Forfeitable: Unused days are lost at the end of the year — they do not accumulate and cannot be converted to cash.
key_terms_explained.Deemed approved: Treated in law as approved because the employer failed to act within the deadline.
key_terms_explained.Constructive dismissal: Making conditions so intolerable that an employee is forced to resign.
key_terms_explained.Summary proceedings: A simplified hearing process, faster than a full trial.
key_terms_explained.Small and micro enterprises: Business size classifications used in Philippine law; entities in these classes are exempt from this act.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Sha'ban 21, 1446 / 20 February 2025, approved by the Chief Minister on 3 March 2025.

for_employees: Apply to your employer or head of agency
Provide reasonable documentation if required — a death certificate, obituary, or proof of relationship
for_employers: Grant 7 days of paid bereavement leave annually, unless exempt as a small or micro enterprise
Act on an application within five working days, or it is deemed approved
Take no adverse action against an employee for using the leave

what_is_prohibited: Taking adverse employment action against an employee for availing of bereavement leave — including termination, constructive dismissal, demotion of any kind, or issuing an unsatisfactory performance rating.
Unjustified denial of, or refusal to act on, a bereavement leave application.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence committed by an employee.
penalties.for_employers: The act sets no fine or imprisonment. Its remedies are procedural: an unacted application is deemed approved, and unjustified denial can be heard and decided by the Minister of Labor and Employment through summary proceedings.
penalties.for_public_officers: Complaints against responsible officers in the public sector are governed by the Revised Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service.

where_to_complain.private_sector: The Minister of Labor and Employment (MOLE), or a duly authorised MOLE hearing officer, who may hear and decide through summary proceedings after due notice
where_to_complain.public_sector: Under the Revised Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service
where_to_complain.note: Section 9 gives an express legal remedy, which most acts in this registry do not.

everyday_scenarios: Fatima's mother dies on a Thursday. She applies for bereavement leave; because Saturdays, Sundays and holidays are excluded, her 7 days are seven working days.
Omar submits an application and hears nothing. Five working days after his employer received it, the application is deemed approved by operation of law.
A worker is given a poor performance rating after taking bereavement leave. Section 8 bars exactly that, and the denial or retaliation can be brought to the Minister of Labor and Employment.
A shop with a handful of staff classified as a micro enterprise is exempt from granting the leave under Section 4.
An employee's company already offers 10 days. The non-diminution clause means the more beneficial policy stands.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Bangsamoro Bereavement Leave Act of 2025”.

Section 2 — Policy: the Bangsamoro Government recognises the unique and societal aspects of bereavement and shall foster a workplace culture that upholds the welfare of its people, alongside improving public morals, promoting full employment and preserving the well-being of inhabitants.

Section 3 — Any employee, regardless of employment status, in the private or public sector within the BARMM is entitled to 7 days of bereavement leave with pay annually, following the death of an immediate family member. Saturdays, Sundays and holidays are excluded in computing the leave period.
Section 4 — Only employees engaged in an employer-employee relationship are entitled. Entities classified as small and micro enterprises are exempt from granting the leave.

Section 5 — Immediate family means the employee's legitimate spouse or spouses; biological or adoptive parents or legal guardians; legitimate parents-in-law; biological or adoptive children or legal wards; or full-blood siblings. The employer may require reasonable documentation, including a death certificate, obituary, or proof of relationship.
Section 6 — Leave not availed of is non-cumulative and non-convertible to cash.
Section 7 — Nothing in the act diminishes more beneficial existing benefits under laws, contracts, agreements, or company policies.

Section 8 — Availing of the leave shall not be a ground for adverse action by the employer, including termination, constructive dismissal, demotion of any kind, or the issuance of an unsatisfactory performance rating.

Section 9 — An application not acted upon within five working days of receipt by the head of agency or the employer is deemed approved. On complaint of an aggrieved private sector employee, the Minister of Labor and Employment or an authorised hearing officer may hear and decide, through summary proceedings after due notice, any matter involving unjustified denial or refusal to act. Public sector complaints follow the Revised Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service.
Section 10 — MOLE shall coordinate with the Civil Service Commission for the BARMM in issuing implementing rules within 60 days of effectivity.
Section 13 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation.

who_benefits: Employees in the public and private sectors across the BARMM
impact.figures_note: The act appropriates no funds. Its figures are entitlements: 7 days of paid leave annually, and a 5-working-day deadline for acting on an application.

citizen_questions.q: How many days do I actually get?
citizen_questions.a: 7 days with pay each year. Saturdays, Sundays and holidays are excluded from the count, so it is seven working days.

citizen_questions.q: Does it matter if I am contractual or casual?
citizen_questions.a: No. Section 3 says any employee 'regardless of employment status', provided you are in an employer-employee relationship.
Your legitimate spouse or spouses; biological or adoptive parents or legal guardians; legitimate parents-in-law; biological or adoptive children or legal wards; and full-blood siblings.

citizen_questions.q: What if my employer ignores my application?
citizen_questions.a: After five working days from receipt without action, the application is deemed approved by operation of law.

citizen_questions.q: Can I be punished for taking it?
citizen_questions.a: No. Section 8 bars termination, constructive dismissal, demotion of any kind, and unsatisfactory performance ratings on that ground.
No. Entities classified as small and micro enterprises are exempt from granting the leave.

citizen_questions.q: Can I save up unused days or cash them out?
citizen_questions.a: No. The leave is non-cumulative and non-convertible to cash — which is why the title calls it forfeitable.
Private sector: the Minister of Labor and Employment or an authorised hearing officer, through summary proceedings. Public sector: the Revised Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service.
